title: Tetralogy of Fallot: Anatomy and Pathophysiology
subject: ss-paediatric-cardiology

steps.say: All four defects of this tetralogy trace back to one developmental error: the outlet septum drifts forward and crowds the right ventricular outflow.
steps.tx: Embryology centres on **infundibular septal deviation (tetralogy four components)**. The four classic components of Tetralogy of Fallot result from anterocephalad (forward and upward) deviation of the infundibular septum: large subaortic ventricular septal defect, overriding aorta, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, and right ventricular hypertrophy.

vis.caption: Key cyanotic congenital heart defects: Tetralogy of Fallot and Transposition of the Great Arteries. Image: National Heart Lung and Blood Institute (NIH), CC0/PD, Wikimedia Commons.
vis.alt: Anatomical diagrams of Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) showing four defects and D-Transposition of the Great Arteries (TGA) with transposed vessels.

steps.say: The same diagnosis can look pink or deeply blue, because one variable, the tightness of the outflow obstruction, sets the whole physiology.
steps.tx: Physiology follows **RVOT obstruction severity, the determinant of cyanosis**. The severity of subpulmonic and valvular right ventricular outflow obstruction determines the magnitude of right to left shunt and degree of cyanosis, so mild obstruction presents as a pink Fallot while severe obstruction produces profound desaturation.

rows: Net left to right across the defect
Pink Fallot with systolic murmur only
Deep cyanosis dependent on ductal flow

steps.say: The chest film in this condition is so distinctive that generations of students have learned it as a wooden shoe.
steps.tx: Radiography shows the **boot shaped heart**. Chest radiograph classically shows a boot shaped heart (coeur en sabot, French for wooden shoe) with an upturned apex due to right ventricular hypertrophy and a concave pulmonary bay from the small underfilled pulmonary trunk.

left.title: Boot Shape Components
points: Upturned cardiac apex lifted by hypertrophied right ventricle
Concave main pulmonary artery segment with oligemic lung fields
Right aortic arch visible in one quarter of patients

right.title: Bedside Correlation
points: Cyanosis severity parallels the degree of outflow obstruction
Single second sound reflects inaudible pulmonary closure
Right ventricular heave palpable at the left sternal edge

steps.say: A quarter of these children carry their aortic arch on the opposite side, a clue that changes how you read the film and plan surgery.
steps.tx: Arch sidedness matters as a **right aortic arch**. A right sided aortic arch is present in approximately **25 percent** of patients with Tetralogy of Fallot, alerting the surgeon to mirror image branching and an aberrant left subclavian course before repair or shunt surgery.

nodes.label: Note absent left sided aortic knuckle with right paratracheal density
Confirm arch sidedness and branching with echocardiography
Define coronary origins since anomalous coronaries alter the repair
Map arch anatomy on CT before sternotomy or shunt placement

steps.say: Behind some cases sits a tiny missing piece of chromosome 22, and its likelihood jumps sharply when the pulmonary valve is absent or atretic.
steps.tx: Genetics involves **chromosome 22q11 deletion (22q11.2 microdeletion)**. Microdeletion of 22q11.2 (DiGeorge or velocardiofacial syndrome) occurs in **15%** of isolated Tetralogy of Fallot and up to **40-50%** of Fallot with pulmonary atresia or absent pulmonary valve, warranting fluorescence testing and calcium and immune screening.

rows: Serum calcium, T cell counts, palate review
Full DiGeorge workup with renal ultrasound

steps.say: Watch an older unrepaired child at play and you will see them instinctively crouch down, a posture that cleverly replumbs their circulation.
steps.tx: Posture exploits the **squatting posture**. Children with Tetralogy of Fallot learn to squat during exertion to increase systemic vascular resistance, thereby decreasing right to left shunting and promoting pulmonary blood flow, which relieves breathlessness faster than rest alone, and this simple posture often aborts early desaturation before any medicine is needed.

left.title: Effect of Squatting
points: Kinking femoral arteries raises systemic vascular resistance
Higher aortic pressure opposes right to left shunting
More right ventricular blood reaches the lungs for oxygenation

right.title: Effect of Crying or Exertion
points: Falling systemic resistance and rising catecholamines worsen obstruction
Right to left shunt increases with deepening cyanosis
May precipitate a hypercyanotic spell needing knee chest positioning

steps.say: Here is a classic examination trap: the loud murmur comes from the narrow outflow, while the large hole itself makes no sound at all.
steps.tx: Auscultation reflects an **RVOT stenosis murmur (auscultation in TOF)**. The murmur in Tetralogy of Fallot is caused solely by right ventricular outflow tract stenosis, a systolic ejection murmur at the mid to upper left sternal border, while the ventricular septal defect is large and non restrictive (silent) with equal ventricular pressures.

nodes.label: Equal biventricular pressures render the large VSD silent
Turbulent ejection across the stenotic outflow generates the murmur
Softer murmur with deeper cyanosis signals tighter obstruction
Absent murmur with profound cyanosis suggests outflow atresia

steps.say: Finally, listen to the second sound: in this lesion it loses its normal split and arrives as a single snap.
steps.tx: Heart sounds show a **single second sound (single S2)**. The second heart sound is typically single because the pulmonary component (P2) is markedly delayed and inaudible, leaving only aortic closure, a finding that complements the ejection murmur and boot shaped silhouette in clinching the bedside diagnosis.
